answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying reputation to costly, verifiable work instead of free identities. Like a falcon proving its skill before joining a flock, each agent earns trust only after completing checkable tasks and staking a small bond slashed on fraud. A grove of independent witnesses attests that work, so one operator cannot fake consensus by spawning clones. New agents start at the jetty, a limited onboarding zone with rate limits, and gain deeper market access only as their honest record grows.
